:Judgment:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.5,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 22062020 at about 5.15 p.m., the Petitioner was travelling as a passenger in an autorickshaw bearing No.KA02 C7108 on KanakapuraSathanur road.
When the said auto reached near Battalugundappana temple, a two wheeler bearing No.KA07V418 which was ridden by its rider from the opposite direction of the auto in a rash and negligent manner dashed against autorickshaw.

Due to the impact,
the petitioner and her copassenger fell down from the auto.
As auto turtled and thereby the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries to her head and all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner took first aid treatment at Kanakapura Government Hospital and thereafter took treatment at NIMHANS hospital and at Sevakshethra hospital of Bengaluru wherein, she took treatment as an inpatient from 26.06.2020 to 01.07.2020.

For her treatment she has spent more than Rs.1,00,000/.
3.
Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and she was working as the tailor and was earning Rs.15,000/ per month.
Due to the accident, she has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.

4. The Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending scooter and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the scooter and therefore, both the Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, the Respondents made appearance through their respective learned advocates.
However, only Respondent No.2 contested the petition by filing written statement in detail.
Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner.
The narration of the occurrence of accident as stated by the petitioner is also denied.
This respondent admits to have issued the policy to the offending two wheeler and contends that same is subject to the terms and conditions.
This respondent also denies the involvement of offending two wheeler in the alleged accident.

It is Rita vs Sanjay S.R on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24056107/
2 also contended that the rider of two wheeler did not possess valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.

sentences.text: Apart from that, it is contended that the driver of autorickshaw also contributed in occurrence of the accident and that there is no negligent act from the part of the rider of two wheeler.
On all these grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that she sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 22.06.2020 at about 6.00 p.m. near Battalugundappa Temple, Sathanur Kanakapura road, NH 209, Ramanagara, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent riding of rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA07V418?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
7. In order to substantiate her case, the Petitioner got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked 15 documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.15.
She also examined a doctor as P.W.2 and got marked 3 documents as per Ex.P16 to 18 and closed her side evidence.
8. On the other hand, Respondent No.2 examined its Assistant Manager as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 to 7 and closed it's side evidence.
PW.1 and 2 have been cross examined at length by the learned advocate for respondent No.2.
RW.1 is also cross examined at length by the learned advocate for petitioner.
9. Heard the arguments of the learned advocate for the Petitioner and of the learned advocate for the Respondent No.2.
In support of his oral submission, the learned advocate for the petitioner also submitted written arguments and also relied upon the following decisions.

1.2023 ACJ 1708 between United India Insurance company Ltd., Vs. N.Praveena and others.
2. 2020 (3) AKR 210 between Hanumantharayappa and others Vs. Chinnappa Sabastin and another.

10. Upon hearing the arguments, upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited by the respective parties and having considered the materials made available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No. 2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS Rita vs Sanjay S.R on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24056107/
3 11.
Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that she was travelling as a passenger in an autorickshaw bearing No.KA02C7108 on the fatal day at about 5.15 p.m. on Kanakapura Sathanur main road.

According to her at about 6 p.m., the rider of offending vehicle who came from the opposite direction of the said auto in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to auto and same resulted in occurrence of accident.
She has further asserted that due to the impact, the autorickshaw turtled and petitioner fell down and thereby she sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement.
12. To prove this aspect during her examination in chief she relied upon the documents Ex. P.1 to 8.

Upon careful consideration of the contents of the said documents, it is clear that in connection to the alleged incident, the Kanakapura Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.21/2020 against the rider of offending motor cycle bearing No.KA07V418.

The spot sketch furnished along with Ex.
P.3 document gives a clear picture of the fact that the rider of two wheeler having proceeded to the extreme right of his path caused accident against the autorickshaw which was properly moving on its path.
The document Ex.P.5 makes it clear that there is involvement of the autorickshaw in which the petitioner was a passenger and the offending motor cycle in the accident on that particular day.
The charge sheet document Ex.P.6 makes it clear that after thorough investigation the IO has charge sheeted the rider of offending two wheeler for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
The documents Ex.P.7 and 8 gives a clear picture of the fact that the petitioner has sustained injuries on her head and on the other parts of the body.
There is no dispute of the fact that PW.1 has been cross examined at length by the learned advocate for Respondent No.2.
However, no such evidence which could take away the assertion of the petitioner has been elicited during her cross examination.
Such being the case, the oral evidence of PW.1 stands corroborated with the documentary evidence as referred above.

All these factors constitute that on account of the rash and negligent riding of the offending motor cycle bearing No.KA07V418 by its rider on the fatal day the petitioner has sustained grievous injury of the nature of permanent disablement.
In addition to this, the evidence given by PW.2 also supports the case of petitioner that as a result of RTA the petitioner has sustained the injuries.

Though suggestions have been made to PW.2 to the effect that in order to help the petitioner in getting higher compensation PW.2 has made assessment of disabilities at a higher rate, such suggestions have been categorically denied by PW.2.
All these factors leads this Tribunal to answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.

Accordingly, I proceed to answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
13. Issue No. 2 : In the above paragraphs, while giving findings to the issue No.1, this Tribunal has made several observations and has arrived at a conclusion that the cause of injuries sustained by the petitioner is on account of the negligence on the part of rider of offending two wheeler.

Hence,
certainly the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
14. In the back drop of the above observations, now let us analyse as to the quantum of compensation to which the petitioner is entitled to and from whom.

In this regard, the respondent No.2 since the date of contesting the petition has taken up a stand that the rider of offending vehicle did not possess a valid and effective driving licence to ride the same.

According to respondent No.2,
as there is violation of terms and conditions of policy it is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Keeping this factor in mind, if careful consideration is given to the police records made Rita vs Sanjay S.R on 15 March, 2024
Indian

Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24056107/
4 available, it is clear that the IO has charge sheeted the rider of two wheeler alleging that he has committed offences punishable u/s 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
There is no such allegation of the fact that the rider did not possess valid and effective driving licence.

15. It is pertinent to note that during the course of investigation the IO appears to have issued a notice as per law to the owner of the offending two wheeler and secured reply from him as per Ex.R.3.

Upon careful consideration of Ex.R.3 it is clear that the owner has admitted the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle did not possess valid and effective driving licence as on the date of occurrence accident.
However, it is for the best reasons known to the IO the accused is not alleged of commission of offence of riding two wheeler on a public way without holding valid and effective driving licence.
16. It is also pertinent to note that to contradict the case of the petitioner, respondent No.2 got examined its witness as RW.1.
The affidavit averments of RW.1 reiterates the contentions raised by the respondent No.2 in the objections.
However, though the witness RW.1 admits to have no personal knowledge regarding the documents which are got marked through him.
But, as the witness deposed that he is giving evidence based on the documents submitted to the court, as the documents have been marked through RW.1 same may be considered for appreciation.

As the owner of vehicle though made appearance did not choose to contest the petition and inspite of best efforts made by the respondent No.2 through a notice issued to the owner on 09.02.2021 to furnish the documents mentioned therein and inspite of service of the same there is no response from the owner of the offending vehicle, it may be presumed that the rider of offending vehicle did not possess valid and effective driving licence to ride the same on a fatal day.
17. I have carefully considered the principles held in the decisions referred and relied upon by the petitioner as noted above.
I have also given consideration of the date of occurrence of accident which is much prior to the date of amendment brought to the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act.

In the light of the principles held by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in those decisions and also keeping in mind the fact that there is admission of respondent No.2 regarding the issuance of policy and its validity as on the date of accident, this Tribunal is of the view that it is just and proper to direct the respondent No.2 to pay compensation and to recover the same from respondent No.1 through process of law.
With all these observations, this Tribunal is of the view that the petitioner is entitled to claim compensation from the respondent No.1 and 2 jointly and severally.
18. The petitioner has asserted that she was a tailor by profession and was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/ per month.
In this regard, admittedly she has not furnished any supportive document.
Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
If same is considered keeping in mind the date of occurrence of accident, petitioner's notional income is taken at Rs.14,500/p.m. for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
19. According to the petitioner she was 36 ye ars old at the time of incident.
To prove her age, she has furnished her Aadhar card at Ex.P.15.
Upon consideration of the same, same reflects the date of birth of the petitioner as on 01.01.1984.
The accident occurred on 22.06.2020.

Hence, the age of the Rita vs Sanjay S.R on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24056107/
5 Petitioner as on the date of accident was 36 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
20. According to the petitioner, she has suffered such injuries in the accident of the nature of permanent disablement.
Same has been deposed by her even during her evidence.
To support this factor, she got examined PW.2.
In his evidence PW.2 has stated that the petitioner is suffering from injuries and the disability for whole body is arrived at 17%.
During her cross examination, PW.2 admits to have not undergone any surgery but to have got treated only on the line of conservative treatment.
During the cross examination of PW.2, he admits that the petitioner got treated at NIMHANS Hospital as an outpatient.
He admits to have only assessed the disabilities of the patient during his examination.
There is also admission of the fact that PW.2 has not gone through any medical records pertaining to the petitioner except the wound certificate and discharge summary of Sevakshethra hospital.
PW.2 admits that petitioner has not undergone any surgery.
He also admits that the petitioner has taken only conservative line of treatment.
21. It is pertinent to note that the doctor who got examined as PW.2 is ENT specialist.
According to the petitioner, she has sustained grievous injuries to her head in the fatal accident.
If consideration is given to the document at Ex. P.4, it reflects that the doctor who has issued the same opined that the injuries mentioned in Ex. P.4 at Sl.No.2 and 3 are grievous in nature.
The wound certificate Ex.P.4 discloses that the petitioner sustained following injuries.
1. Deep fresh cut wound frontal region 15 cm x 3 cm. sutured with 5 pressure stitch.
2. Left eye swelling 3.
Right nose bleeding 4.
Small drain nose 5.
Abrasion left knee joint 6.
Cut lacerated right knee 4 x 3 cm. 6 sutured applied.
22. In the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in (2011) 1 SCC 344 - Rajkumar Vs.Ajay Kumar and another.

entities.text: (2011) 1 SCC 344 - Rajkumar Vs.Ajay Kumar and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Apex Court held as follows:
23.
The Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and if so the extent of such permanent disability.
Hence, the Tribunal shall consider and decide the same with reference to the evidence.
i) Whether the disablement is permanent or temporary ii) If the disablement is permanent, whether there is total permanent disablement or permanent partial disablement.

Rita vs Sanjay S.R on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24056107/
6 iii) If the disablement percentage is expressed with reference to any specific limb, then the effect of such disablement of limb on the functioning of the entire body, i.e., the permanent disability suffered by the person.

entities.text: Rita vs Sanjay S.R on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the Tribunal concludes that there is no permanent disability then there is no question of proceeding further and determining the loss of future earning capacity.
But, if the Tribunal concludes that there is a permanent disability, then it will proceed to ascertain its extent.
Ascertainment of the effect of permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.
The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on inspite of the permanent disability and what the claimant could not do as a result of permanent disability.
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident and also the age.

The third step is to find out whether the claimant is total disabled from earning any kind of livelihood or whether inspite of the permanent disability the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions which he was earlier doing or whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions, but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood.
24.
By applying the said precedent to the present case on hand, from the petition averments it can be ascertained that the petitioner was a tailor by profession.
To perform the said profession proper eyesight, proper usage of both the hands and legs is necessary.
In this case, PW.2 deposed that there is fracture of cervical vertebra 1 and also there is complaint of pain in movement of neck.
After assessing the disability, the doctor PW.2 arrived the total disability of the petitioner at 17% to the whole body.

Upon consideration of the fact that the petitioner was a tailor, this Tribunal is of the opinion that she may have to sit for longer duration for which she needs support of proper function of neck, back and her legs and hands.
However, there are no such medical records to show that the petitioner has underwent surgery.
If that is considered, the disability assessed by the doctor appears to be at the higher rate.
Keeping in mind the injuries sustained by the petitioner, there are chances of loss of her future earnings.
However, the Tribunal is of the view that if disability is considered at 8% it would be proper and reasonable.
25. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
26.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of Rs.35,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

Rita vs Sanjay S.R on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24056107/
7
II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES:
27. Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
28. The Petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in her evidence that she was admitted as an inpatient.
Further, P.W.2 Dr.S.U.Shiva Prakash has also reiterated the same in his evidence.

The medical records disclose the fact that petitioner got admitted as an inpatient from 26.06.2020 to 01.07.2020.
29.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.29,000/ under this head (@ Rs.14,500/ per month).
 IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
30.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also she might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for her conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.5,000/ towards attendants charges, Rs.5,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.5,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/ under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
31. The Petitioner has deposed that she spent more than Rs.1,00,000/ towards medical expenses and other expenses.
In order to prove this fact, she has produced 40 medical bills at Ex.P.13 amounting to Rs.38,512/.
I have perused the same carefully.
They appears to be acceptable.
Moreover, there is no serious dispute regarding the said medical bills.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.38,500/ as a compensation under this head.
VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :

32. The Petitioner has deposed in her evidence that due to the injuries sustained by her in the accident, she has suffered permanent disablement and she is suffering from severe pain at fractured Rita vs Sanjay S.R on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24056107/
8 area, cannot bear any weight, cannot use Indian toilet, cannot squat on floor, cannot climb stairs,
stand stand or walk for more than 10 minutes, using waterbed to sleep, get severe headache,
frequent giddiness, cannot go under sunshine, cannot hear from right ear and lost smelling sense.
33.

Further, the Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr.S.U.Shiva Prakash as P.W.2 who also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident and examination he made.
Further, he got marked clinical notes, 2 xrays at Ex.P.16 to 18.
He assessed total whole body disability at 17%.

34. Hence, having regard to the medical records placed on record and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and by considering the nature of her work, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 8% would be just and proper.
As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 15.

With multiplier of 15, income of Rs.14,500/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 8%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.2,08,800/ (Rs.14,500/ x 12 =
1,75,000/, Rs.1,74,000/x 15 x 8/100 = 2,08,800/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,08,800/ which is rounded off to Rs.2,08,800/ under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
35.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 35,000/
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 20,000/
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 15,000/ diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs. 38,500/
5. Loss of income during the Rs. 29,000/ laid up period 6. Loss of Future income Rs.2,08,800/ Total Rs.3,46,300/ Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.3,46,300/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

36. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA07 V418.
There are observations made above that the said rider did not possess valid and effective driving licence.

However, if the date of occurrence of accident is taken into consideration keeping in mind the fact that the owner of the vehicle though made appearance failed to contest the petition,
the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally held liable to compensate the petitioner.

Rita vs Sanjay S.R on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24056107/
9
However, the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to pay compensation to the petitioner and may recover the same from respondent No.1 as per the process of law.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
37. ISSUE No. 3 :

In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No. 1 and 2 U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.3,46,300/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
The respondent No.2 may recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle i.e., respondent No.1 as per due process of law.
After the deposit of the Award amount and interest being made by the Respondent No.2, entire award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E payment and after proper identification.

The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw Award accordingly.

There is no such allegation of the fact that the rider did not possess valid and effective driving licence.
Upon careful consideration of Ex.R.3 it is clear that the owner has admitted the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle did not possess valid and effective driving licence as on the date of occurrence accident.
However, it is for the best reasons known to the IO the accused is not alleged of commission of offence of riding two wheeler on a public way without holding valid and effective driving licence.
In the light of the principles held by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in those decisions and also keeping in mind the fact that there is admission of respondent No.2 regarding the issuance of policy and its validity as on the date of accident, this Tribunal is of the view that it is just and proper to direct the respondent No.2 to pay compensation and to recover the same from respondent No.1 through process of law.
18. The petitioner has asserted that she was a tailor by profession and was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/ per month.
In this regard, admittedly she has not furnished any supportive document.
Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
If same is considered keeping in mind the date of occurrence of accident, petitioner's notional income is taken at Rs.14,500/p.m. for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
19. According to the petitioner she was 36 ye ars old at the time of incident.
The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on inspite of the permanent disability and what the claimant could not do as a result of permanent disability.
The third step is to find out whether the claimant is total disabled from earning any kind of livelihood or whether inspite of the permanent disability the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions which he was earlier doing or whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions, but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood.
24.
By applying the said precedent to the present case on hand, from the petition averments it can be ascertained that the petitioner was a tailor by profession.
To perform the said profession proper eyesight, proper usage of both the hands and legs is necessary.
If that is considered, the disability assessed by the doctor appears to be at the higher rate.
Keeping in mind the injuries sustained by the petitioner, there are chances of loss of her future earnings.
However, the Tribunal is of the view that if disability is considered at 8% it would be proper and reasonable.

30.
In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.5,000/ towards attendants charges, Rs.5,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.5,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.

37. ISSUE No. 3 :

ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No. 1 and 2 U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.3,46,300/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.

After the deposit of the Award amount and interest being made by the Respondent No.2, entire award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E payment and after proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
